findings.claim: The delivery-review-2 note that no ops key is declared in the matrix is inaccurate. OPS_SURFACE_RULES declares sixteen ops keys and six of the generated resource identities reuse them exactly: agent-profile read and create, operational-device read and create, team read and create, shift read and create, homologation read, application-version read, evidence read and external-query create. Those generated routes are therefore reachable by field-agent, field-supervisor, processing-operator, traffic-authority and technical-admin, not only by a global admin. Only one route is a real widening: the handwritten controller exposed GET shifts/:id and POST shifts but no collection read, while the generated controller adds GET /v1/ops/field/shifts under the same ops:shift:read key. Every generated update and delete key is absent from the matrix and stays admin-only, and RLS still scopes every read by tenant, so the surface remains fail closed where no grant exists.
findings.fix: When WP-T2 wires policy for ops, add positive and exhaustive negative role tests for the eight inherited keys and decide explicitly whether ops:shift:read should cover the collection read or whether the generated shift list needs its own key.
